sources.title: Census 2016 Small Area Population Statistics, means of travel (SAP2016T11T1PROV)
Census 2022 Small Area Population Statistics, means of travel (SAP2022T11T1PROV)

key_fact: At the 2022 census, 55% of pupils and students went to school or college by car, 23% walked and 3.0% cycled.

title: How people travel to work
subtitle: Share of people travelling to work, by main means of travel, census 2016 and 2022.

sources.title: Census 2016 Small Area Population Statistics, means of travel (SAP2016T11T1PROV)
Census 2022 Small Area Population Statistics, means of travel (SAP2022T11T1PROV)

key_fact: At the 2022 census, 64% of people travelling to work drove, 10% walked and 3% cycled.

title: Businesses using AI
subtitle: Share of businesses with 10 or more staff that use at least one AI technology, by size, 2023 to 2025.
key_fact: 20% of businesses with 10 or more staff used AI in 2025, up from 8% in 2023. Large businesses were the most likely to use it, at 58%.

title: Businesses using AI across the EU
subtitle: Share of businesses with 10 or more staff that use at least one AI technology, EU countries, 2025.

sources.title: Enterprise use of Artificial Intelligence and Cloud Computing (BIIESA20)

key_fact: In 2025, 19.6% of businesses in Ireland with 10 or more staff used AI, compared with 20.0% across the EU.

title: Electricity used by data centres
subtitle: Data centres' share of all metered electricity used in Ireland, 2015 to 2025.
key_fact: Data centres used 23% of all metered electricity in Ireland in 2025, up from 5% in 2015.

title: Electricity used by data centres and other customers
subtitle: Metered electricity consumption, terawatt hours (TWh), 2015 to 2025.
key_fact: Data centres used 7.7 TWh of electricity in 2025, 6.2 times as much as in 2015. Use by all other customers rose by 8% over the same period.

title: Data centre planning applications by county
subtitle: Planning applications to councils that mention a data centre, by county, 2017 to May 2026.

sources.publisher: Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage
sources.title: National planning applications register (Planning Application Points)

key_fact: Dublin had 56 of the 90 planning applications that mention a data centre from 2017 to May 2026. Applications were made in 11 of the 26 counties.

title: How familiar people are with the term AI
subtitle: Share of adults by how well they understand the term artificial intelligence (AI), 2025.

sources.title: Respondents familiarity with the term artificial intelligence (AI) (TRA226)
Respondents familiarity with the term artificial intelligence (AI), by age (TRA227)

key_fact: In 2025, 56% of adults said they understood the term AI well enough to explain it to others. The share ranged from 82% of people aged 18 to 29 to 38% of those aged 50 and over.

title: Use of generative AI by age
subtitle: Share of people who used generative AI tools in the previous three months, by age, Ireland and the EU, 2025.

sources.title: Individuals - use of generative AI tools (isoc_ai_iaiu)

key_fact: In 2025, 66% of people aged 16 to 24 in Ireland had used generative AI tools in the previous three months, compared with 11% of those aged 65 to 74.

title: Use of generative AI across the EU
subtitle: Share of people aged 16 to 74 who used generative AI tools in the previous three months, EU countries, 2025.

sources.title: Individuals - use of generative AI tools (isoc_ai_iaiu)

key_fact: In 2025, 45% of people aged 16 to 74 in Ireland had used generative AI tools in the previous three months, compared with 33% across the EU. Ireland's share was the 5th highest of the 27 EU countries.

title: Poverty and deprivation by age
subtitle: Share of people at risk of poverty, experiencing deprivation, and in consistent poverty, by age, 2025.

sources.title: Income, poverty and deprivation rates, by age group (SIA61)

key_fact: In 2025, 14.8% of people aged 65 and over were at risk of poverty, and 16.9% of children.

title: Poverty and deprivation by type of household
subtitle: Share of people at risk of poverty, experiencing deprivation, and in consistent poverty, by type of household, 2025.

sources.title: Income, poverty and deprivation rates, by household composition (SIA64)

key_fact: In 2025, 48.7% of people in one-parent households experienced deprivation, compared with 12.3% in households of two adults with one to three children.

title: Poverty and deprivation by work status
subtitle: Share of people aged 16 and over at risk of poverty, experiencing deprivation, and in consistent poverty, by main economic status, 2025.

sources.title: Income, poverty and deprivation rates, by principal economic status (SIA62)

key_fact: In 2025, 29.3% of unemployed people were at risk of poverty, compared with 5.7% of people in work.

title: Children at risk of poverty or social exclusion across the EU
subtitle: Share of children aged under 18 at risk of poverty or social exclusion, EU countries, 2025.

sources.title: Persons at risk of poverty or social exclusion (ilc_peps01n)

key_fact: In 2025, 23.7% of children in Ireland were at risk of poverty or social exclusion, compared with 24.3% across the EU. Ireland's rate was the 9th highest of the 27 EU countries.

title: Children in low-income households by type of family
subtitle: Share of children aged under 18 living in a low-income household, by type of family, 2022.

sources.title: Children aged under 18 living in low-income households (CCLIH09)

key_fact: In 2022, 30% of children living with a lone mother and 29% of those living with a lone father were in low-income households, compared with 12% of children of married couples.

title: Children in low-income households by parents' work
subtitle: Share of children aged under 18 living in a low-income household, by how many parents are at work, 2022.

sources.title: Children aged under 18 living in low-income households (CCLIH11)

key_fact: In 2022, 62% of children in households where no parent was at work lived on a low income, compared with 4% where two parents were at work.

title: Children in low-income households by county
subtitle: Share of children aged under 18 living in a household with income below 60% of the national median, by county, 2022.

sources.title: Children aged under 18 living in low-income households (CCLIH03)

key_fact: In 2022, 16.1% of children in Ireland lived in low-income households. The share ranged from 28.2% in Donegal to 12.2% in Dublin.

title: Child poverty and deprivation
subtitle: Share of children aged under 18 at risk of poverty, experiencing deprivation, and in consistent poverty, 2020 to 2025.

sources.title: Income, poverty and deprivation rates, by age group (SIA61)

key_fact: In 2025, 16.9% of children were at risk of poverty, 19.6% experienced deprivation and 7.8% were in consistent poverty.

title: Income inequality before and after tax and social welfare
subtitle: Gini coefficient of household income, adjusted for household size, 2020 to 2025.
key_fact: In 2025, the Gini coefficient for household income was 45.5 before tax and social welfare and 27.4 after them.

title: Income inequality across the EU
subtitle: Gini coefficient of disposable household income, EU countries, 2025.

sources.title: Gini coefficient of equivalised disposable income (ilc_di12)

key_fact: In 2025, Ireland's Gini coefficient for disposable income was 27.2, compared with 29.2 for the EU as a whole. It was the 8th lowest of the 27 EU countries.

title: Poverty and deprivation
subtitle: Share of people at risk of poverty, experiencing deprivation, and in consistent poverty, 2020 to 2025.

sources.title: Key national indicators of poverty, deprivation and social exclusion (SIA77)

key_fact: In 2025, 12.6% of people in Ireland were at risk of poverty, 15.1% experienced deprivation and 4.7% were in consistent poverty.

title: Poverty before and after social welfare
subtitle: Share of people at risk of poverty, counting income before and after social welfare payments, 2025.

sources.title: Key national indicators of poverty, deprivation and social exclusion (SIA77)

key_fact: In 2025, 33.2% of people would have been at risk of poverty without social welfare payments, compared with 12.6% after them.

title: Children as a share of the population
subtitle: Children aged under 18 as a share of the population, 1926 to 2026.

sources.title: Population estimates from 1926, by single year of age (PEA11)

key_fact: There were about 1.22 million children aged under 18 in Ireland in 2026, 22% of the population. The highest share in these figures was 37%, in 1966.

title: Children's general health
subtitle: Share of children whose health was described as good or very good, by age, 2025.

sources.title: Self-perceived general health of children aged 3 to 14 years (IHSC01)

key_fact: In 2025, the health of 94% of children aged 3 to 14 was described as good or very good.

title: Children in care by type of placement
subtitle: Number of children in the care of the State, by type of placement, January 2025.

sources.title: Placement type of children in care in January 2025 (EAACC12)

key_fact: There were 5,383 children in care in January 2025. 88% of them were in foster care, including with relatives.

title: Infant mortality in Ireland and the EU
subtitle: Deaths of babies under one year old per 1,000 live births, 1960 to 2024.
key_fact: In 2024, 3.3 babies in every 1,000 born in Ireland died before their first birthday, down from 29.3 in 1960.

title: Babies born with a low birth weight
subtitle: Share of births weighing under 2,500 grams, selected years 2009 to 2023.
key_fact: In 2023, 6.3% of babies born in Ireland weighed under 2,500 grams.

title: Women in senior roles in large companies
subtitle: Women's share of senior roles in large enterprises, 2019 to 2025.
key_fact: In 2025, women held 28% of board seats and 19% of chief executive roles in large companies, up from 20% and 12% in 2019.

title: Women's share of unpaid carers
subtitle: Women as a share of people who give regular unpaid help to someone with a long-lasting health condition, illness or disability, by hours a week, 2022.
key_fact: In 2022, 61% of unpaid carers were women, and 65% of those giving 43 hours or more a week.

title: Women elected to the Dáil
subtitle: Women as a share of TDs elected at general elections, selected Dála, 1918 to 2024.

sources.title: Women and men elected to Dáil Éireann (G0502)

key_fact: 44 women were elected to the Dáil in 2024, 25% of all TDs. 1 woman was elected to the first Dáil in 1918.

title: Employment rates of women and men
subtitle: Share of people aged 20 to 64 in work, women and men, Ireland, 2009 to 2025.

sources.title: Employment and activity by sex and age, annual data (lfsi_emp_a)

key_fact: In 2025, 75.7% of women aged 20 to 64 in Ireland were in work, compared with 84.7% of men. In 2009 the figures were 62.8% and 73.2%.

title: Gender Equality Index by area
subtitle: Gender Equality Index score for each area, out of 100, Ireland and the EU, 2022.

sources.title: Gender Equality Index (European Institute for Gender Equality) (WMI06)

key_fact: In the 2022 Gender Equality Index, Ireland scored highest on health, at 94.6, and lowest on time, at 59.5.

title: Gender Equality Index across the EU
subtitle: Gender Equality Index score, out of 100, EU countries, 2022.

sources.title: Gender Equality Index (European Institute for Gender Equality) (WMI06)

key_fact: Ireland scored 73.4 out of 100 on the Gender Equality Index for 2022, compared with 71.0 for the EU as a whole. Its score was the 9th highest of the 27 EU countries.

title: The gender pay gap in Ireland and the EU
subtitle: Difference between men's and women's average gross hourly earnings, as a percentage of men's, 2007 to 2024.

sources.title: Gender pay gap in unadjusted form (earn_gr_gpgr2)

key_fact: In 2024, women in Ireland earned on average 8.3% less per hour than men, compared with 11.1% across the EU.

title: The gender pay gap across the EU
subtitle: Difference between men's and women's average gross hourly earnings, as a percentage of men's, EU countries, 2024.

sources.title: Gender pay gap in unadjusted form (earn_gr_gpgr2)

key_fact: Ireland's gender pay gap was 8.3% in 2024, compared with 11.1% across the EU. It was the 11th lowest of the 27 EU countries.

title: Women's share of the best-paid jobs
subtitle: Women's share of all jobs and of the best-paid jobs, by annual earnings, 2011 to 2025.

sources.title: Gender representation in employments, by earnings (DEA02)

key_fact: In 2025, women held 49% of all jobs but 28% of the jobs in the top 1% of earnings, up from 18% in 2011.

title: Household electricity prices across the EU
subtitle: Average price of electricity for households, euro per kilowatt hour including taxes, EU countries, first half of 2026.

sources.title: Electricity prices for household consumers, bi-annual data (nrg_pc_204)

key_fact: In the first half of 2026, households in Ireland paid on average €0.387 per kilowatt hour of electricity, including taxes, compared with €0.283 across the EU. Ireland's price was the highest of the 27 EU countries.

title: Where Ireland's electricity comes from
subtitle: Share of electricity generated in Ireland, by source, 1990 to 2024.

sources.title: Gross production of electricity and derived heat by fuel (nrg_bal_peh)

key_fact: In 2024, 37% of the electricity generated in Ireland came from wind and 48% from natural gas. In 1990, 56% came from coal and peat.

title: Reliance on imported energy
subtitle: Net energy imports as a share of all energy used, Ireland and the EU, 1990 to 2024.
key_fact: In 2024, Ireland imported 80% of the energy it used, compared with 57% for the EU as a whole.

title: Renewable electricity across the EU
subtitle: Share of electricity consumption from renewable sources, EU countries, 2025.

sources.title: Share of energy from renewable sources (nrg_ind_ren)

key_fact: In 2025, 41.7% of the electricity used in Ireland came from renewable sources, compared with 49.9% across the EU. Ireland's share was the 12th lowest of the 27 EU countries.

title: Renewable energy in Ireland and the EU
subtitle: Share of energy used that comes from renewable sources, 2004 to 2025.

sources.title: Share of energy from renewable sources (nrg_ind_ren)

key_fact: In 2025, 17.2% of the energy used in Ireland came from renewable sources, up from 2.4% in 2004. The EU figure was 26.2%.

title: Dairy and beef cows
subtitle: Number of dairy cows and other cows in Ireland in December, in millions, 2005 to 2025.
key_fact: There were 1.49 million dairy cows in Ireland in December 2025, up from 1.00 million in 2005. Beef cows fell from 1.11 million to 0.75 million.

title: Dairy farms by county
subtitle: Specialist dairy farms as a share of all farms in each county, 2020.
key_fact: In 2020, 28% of farms in Cork were dairy farms, the highest share of any county, followed by Waterford at 26%. Leitrim had the lowest share, at 1%.

title: Types of farm
subtitle: Share of farms in Ireland, by main type of farming, 2023.
key_fact: There were 133,174 farms in Ireland in 2023. 56% were specialist beef farms, the most common type.

title: Fertiliser sales
subtitle: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium in fertiliser sold in Ireland, in thousands of tonnes, 2000 to 2025.
key_fact: Fertiliser sold in Ireland in 2025 contained 349 thousand tonnes of nitrogen, compared with 408 thousand tonnes in 2000.

title: Food waste
subtitle: Food wasted per person in Ireland and the EU, in kilograms, by where it was wasted, 2023.
key_fact: Ireland wasted 157 kg of food per person in 2023, compared with 129 kg across the EU. Households wasted 42 kg per person.

title: Age of farmers
subtitle: Farm holders in Ireland by age group, 2023.
key_fact: In 2023, 38% of farm holders were aged 65 or over and 4% were under 35. The average age of a farm holder was 57 in 2020, up from 51 in 2000.

title: Farm income
subtitle: Total income from farming in Ireland, in billions of euro at current prices, 1990 to 2025.

sources.title: Value at Current Prices for Output, Input and Income in Agriculture (AEA01)

key_fact: Farm income in Ireland was €4.6 billion in 2025, compared with €1.6 billion in 1990. The lowest in the period was €0.9 billion in 2009.

title: Cattle, sheep and pigs
subtitle: Number of cattle, sheep and pigs on farms in Ireland in December, in millions, 1980 to 2024.

sources.title: Ireland cattle, sheep and pigs December (EIIA18)

key_fact: There were 6.3 million cattle on Irish farms in December 2024, compared with 5.8 million in 1980. Sheep numbers peaked at 6.1 million in 1992.

title: Milk from Irish farms
subtitle: Cows' milk taken in by dairies from farms in Ireland, in billions of litres, 1992 to 2025.

sources.title: Intake of Cows Milk by Milk Processors and Co-Ops (AKA01)

key_fact: Irish dairies took in 8.8 billion litres of milk from Irish farms in 2025, compared with 5.7 billion litres in 2014, the last full year of EU milk quotas.

title: Organic farming across the EU
subtitle: Share of farmed land used for organic farming, EU countries, 2024.
key_fact: In 2024, 5.0% of farmed land in Ireland was organic or being converted to organic. Ireland's share was the 4th lowest of the 25 EU countries.

title: What Irish farms produce
subtitle: Value of goods produced by farms in Ireland, by product, as a share of the total, 2025.

sources.title: Value at Current Prices for Output, Input and Income in Agriculture (AEA01)

key_fact: Milk made up 34% of the value of goods produced by Irish farms in 2025, and cattle 32%. Farms produced goods worth €13.2 billion in total.

title: Types of cyber security incident
subtitle: Share of businesses that had each type of ICT security incident, Ireland and the EU, 2024.
key_fact: In 2024, 1.2% of businesses in Ireland had ICT services go down because of an outside attack such as ransomware, compared with 3.4% across the EU. Hardware or software failures were far more common.

title: Cyber security incidents at businesses
subtitle: Share of businesses that had an ICT security incident, EU countries, 2024.
key_fact: In 2024, 13% of businesses in Ireland had an ICT security incident, compared with 22% across the EU. Ireland's share was the 7th lowest of the 27 EU countries.

title: Defence spending across the EU
subtitle: Government spending on defence per person, in euro, EU countries, 2024.
key_fact: Government spending on defence in Ireland was €157 per person in 2024, compared with €592 across the EU. Ireland's spending was the lowest of the 27 EU countries. It came to 0.1% of GDP, compared with 1.5% across the EU.

title: Defence as a share of government spending
subtitle: Defence as a share of total government spending, Ireland and the EU, 1995 to 2024.
key_fact: Defence made up 0.7% of government spending in Ireland in 2024, compared with 3.0% across the EU. In 1995 it was 2.1% in Ireland.

title: Defence spending in Ireland
subtitle: Government spending on defence in Ireland, in millions of euro at current prices, 1995 to 2024.
key_fact: The Irish government spent €841 million on defence in 2024, compared with €444 million in 1995. The highest in the period was €1,108 million in 2023.

title: Trust in the armed forces
subtitle: Share of people who trust their country's armed forces, OECD Trust Survey countries, 2025.

sources.title: OECD Trust Survey, trust in institutions across countries (TRA312)

key_fact: In 2025, 69% of people in Ireland said they trust the armed forces, compared with an OECD average of 66%. Ireland ranked 14th of the 36 countries with figures.

title: Satisfaction with how elections are run
subtitle: Share of people satisfied with how elections are managed in Ireland, by age and by how they voted at the last general election, 2025.

sources.title: Satisfaction with how elections are managed, by age (TRA269)
Satisfaction with how elections are managed, by voting status (TRA273)

key_fact: In 2025, 77% of people aged 18 to 29 were satisfied with how elections are managed in Ireland, compared with 62% of those aged 30 to 49.

title: Trust in national government across countries
subtitle: Share of people who trust their national government, OECD Trust Survey countries, 2025.

sources.title: OECD Trust Survey, trust in institutions across countries (TRA312)

key_fact: In 2025, 44% of people in Ireland said they trust the national government, compared with an OECD average of 40%. Ireland ranked 13th of the 38 countries with figures.

title: Trust in public institutions
subtitle: Share of people in Ireland who trust each institution, 2025.

sources.title: Trust Survey, trust in people and institutions (TRA102)

key_fact: In 2025, 77% of people in Ireland said they trust the electoral system, compared with 44% for the government and 27% for political parties.

title: Turnout at elections
subtitle: Turnout at Dáil and European Parliament elections in Ireland, 1948 to 2024.
key_fact: Turnout at the 2024 general election was 59.7%, compared with 76.9% in 1969, the highest since 1948. Turnout at the 2024 European Parliament election was 50.1%.

title: Turnout at national elections across the EU
subtitle: Turnout at the most recent national parliamentary election in each EU country.
key_fact: Turnout at Ireland's 2024 general election was 59.7%. Comparing each country's most recent national election, Ireland's turnout was the 7th lowest of the 27 EU countries.

title: Views on voting and elections
subtitle: Share of people in Ireland who hold each view, 2025.

sources.title: Perception of voting as a duty or choice (TRA274)
Trust in the Electoral Commission (An Coimisiún Toghcháin) (TRA306)
Trust Survey, trust in people and institutions (TRA102)

key_fact: In 2025, 79% of people in Ireland saw voting as a duty rather than a choice, and 78% said they trust the Electoral Commission.
